name: Marxist feminism
summary: Marxist feminism applies Marx's analysis of class and capital to women's oppression, arguing that it arose with private property and the monogamous family and is sustained by capitalism's reliance on women's unpaid domestic and reproductive labour. It holds that women's liberation requires bringing women into public production, socialising housework and childcare, and ending capitalism, rather than winning equality inside the existing order. Strands differ on whether to demand wages for housework or its socialisation, and on how far patriarchy is a separate system from capital.
scope: Represents the mainstream Marxist and socialist-feminist tradition from Engels's Origin of the Family (1884) and the socialist women's movement of Zetkin and Kollontai through the 1970s domestic-labour debate (Benston, Dalla Costa and James, Vogel) and dual-systems theory (Hartmann). It excludes liberal, radical-separatist and post-structuralist feminisms. Where strands differ (wages for housework versus socialised care; unified versus dual systems), the profile follows the consensus that class transformation is necessary for liberation and records splits as low confidence or neutral.

keyFigures.name: Friedrich Engels
keyFigures.role: Author of The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State, the founding Marxist account of women's subjugation.

keyFigures.name: Mariarosa Dalla Costa
keyFigures.role: Co-author of the 1972 pamphlet arguing housework is productive labour for capital and founder of the Wages for Housework movement.

keyFigures.name: Clara Zetkin
keyFigures.role: Socialist leader who rejected cross-class feminist alliances and organised working women within the labour movement.

sources.title: The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State, chapter 2, part 4
sources.author: Friedrich Engels (1884)
sources.usedFor: Property and women's subjugation, public industry, socialised housework, free marriage, class struggle and materialist history.

sources.title: The Power of Women and the Subversion of the Community
sources.author: Mariarosa Dalla Costa and Selma James (1972)
sources.usedFor: Housework as productive labour for capital, wages for housework, critique of equal pay and reformism, refusal of work.

sources.title: Feminist Perspectives on Class and Work
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Debates on domestic labour, dual systems, state and public patriarchy, socialised care and revolution.

sources.title: Marxist feminism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview, Zetkin and Kollontai on cross-class alliances, Benston and Morton on family labour, organising in labour movements.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Marxist feminists want social reproduction, including care of the sick, shifted from private households to public provision, so a state-guaranteed health service follows from their case for socialised care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not a central demand, but a higher legal wage floor fits the aim of raising working-class women's pay; Dalla Costa and James warn that equal pay alone leaves capitalist relations intact.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Marxist feminism extends the Marxist critique of capital, which holds that market production for profit depends on unpaid women's labour and cannot deliver liberation.

public-ownership.rationale: Engels expects the means of production to pass into common ownership, which is the precondition for ending the family as the economic unit.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not a stated plank, inferred from class-based redistribution aims; adherents see taxation as a reform short of the transformation they want.

unions-good.rationale: Early Marxist and socialist feminists organised working women inside the labour movement, treating unions as a base for class struggle, though they criticised male-dominated unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Engels traces women's subjugation to the rise of private property and inheritance, so private property is the root problem rather than a right to protect.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation is a reform adherents would accept but see as insufficient; Dalla Costa and James reject strategies that leave capitalist relations in place.

cut-welfare.rationale: Cutting welfare pushes care back onto unpaid women; the SEP notes feminists criticise welfare states as patriarchal but not in order to remove public support.

worker-ownership.rationale: Common ownership of the means of production is Engels's condition for the family ceasing to be society's economic unit; worker control is the Marxist form of this.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the Marxist view of the state as an instrument of the ruling class.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from left-wing opposition to criminalising working-class people.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Never addressed; adherents split between protecting oppressed groups and distrust of state power under capitalism.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on collective self-organisation of women and workers, as in Dalla Costa and James's call for autonomous organising.

state-harmful.rationale: Marxists see the state as a class tool that eventually withers, but expect to use public power to socialise housework, so not simply harmful or unnecessary now.

limit-guns.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from general left positions and concern with violence against women.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from the view of coercive state apparatus as serving the ruling class.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Marxist feminists are split: some treat sex work as exploited labour deserving rights, others as an extreme form of commodified women's bodies; the sources do not settle it.

decide-locally.rationale: Never addressed; the aim is class power rather than a scale of government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the view that crime reflects social conditions.

traditional-family.rationale: Engels argues the monogamous family originated in male property control and that the single family must cease to be the economic unit, so adherents reject it as society's foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not discussed by the classic sources; modern adherents generally support it, though some regard marriage itself as a patriarchal institution.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not in the pages read; inferred from the aim of women's control over reproductive labour and the left-feminist consensus.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist treatment of religion as ideology and Engels's critique of the institutions that sanctify the patriarchal family.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a focus of the classic texts; modern adherents support it, with class as the main frame.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Engels treats the family and women's status as products of social and economic history rather than nature, though the sources do not use the term construct.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred from internationalist class politics; Zetkin and Kollontai organised across class and national lines for women workers.

gradual-change.rationale: Dalla Costa and James reject reformist strategies that leave capitalist relations intact; Engels says full liberation comes only with socialism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from working-class internationalism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Never addressed; adherents distrust institutions of capitalist states but favour international solidarity.

free-trade.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the Marxist view of global capitalism as exploiting women's labour.

nation-first.rationale: Marxist feminism is internationalist: it organises women as part of a worldwide working class, so putting national interest above cooperation is inferred to be rejected.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from anti-imperialism of the socialist left.

open-borders.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from internationalism and solidarity with migrant women workers.

limit-growth.rationale: Never addressed; adherents are split between eco-socialist and productivist Marxists.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from modern left positions and ecofeminist-influenced Marxist writing.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred; Marxist feminists see problems as rooted in social relations, not technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Never addressed and no settled adherent position.

revolution-justified.rationale: Engels states that the wife's liberation requires abolishing capitalist production, and the SEP notes Marxists hold full liberation requires socialism.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from Dalla Costa and James's emphasis on women's own self-organisation over specialist or party direction.

central-planning.rationale: Engels expects housework to become social industry under common ownership, implying planned social production, but the sources do not discuss planning directly.

socialized-markets.rationale: Never addressed; classic Marxists aim to abolish commodity production, but some modern socialists accept markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: The sources never discuss tax reform of this kind, and adherents who want common ownership of land would not centre a single tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Engels ties patriarchal monogamy to inheritance of property by sons, so adherents favour curbing it, though he proposes abolition of inheritance by socialisation rather than taxation.

basic-income.rationale: Not a standard demand, but adherents who favour wages for housework would back guaranteed income for care; some regard it as insufficient.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from support for public control of the economy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Engels wants common ownership, not wide small ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The SEP notes autonomist strands call for ending unpaid domestic work and liberation from work; classical Marxism has money disappearing under communism, though feminists also demand wages in the near term.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from opposition to market-led money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from class-struggle opposition to class partnership.

one-party-rule.rationale: Dalla Costa and James stress autonomous women's organisation beyond party structures, though communist women's movements worked in parties.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred from the socialist opposition to hereditary privilege.

democracy-best.rationale: Never addressed directly; adherents favour democratic self-organisation, but critique bourgeois democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Not discussed directly; inferred from the call for women's self-organised, bottom-up decision-making over representative intermediaries.

workers-councils.rationale: The SEP notes Ferguson's council-socialist vision; classic sources do not centre it.

right-to-secede.rationale: The sources do not address secession, and Marxists usually treat it as a tactical question rather than a principle.

natural-rulers.rationale: Engels argues male supremacy comes from economic supremacy, not nature, which implies rejecting natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Revolution to end capitalist production is endorsed; a blanket ban on political violence is incompatible.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred from socialist and feminist anti-militarism.

separate-church-state.rationale: Never addressed in the pages read; inferred from secular Marxist politics.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred from secular materialism and opposition to religiously sanctioned patriarchy.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist view of the state and from public provision aims.

military-superiority.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from socialist opposition to militarism and the arms race as capitalist-state projects.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from working-class internationalism, which denies that shared ethnicity should define political community.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Engels states that the first class antagonism coincides with the subjugation of the female sex by the male, placing class conflict at the centre of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Dalla Costa and James say equal pay and opportunity leave capitalist relations intact, implying demands go beyond formal equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from anti-colonial left politics.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from anti-imperial class analysis.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from internationalism of class rather than civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Inferred from the collectivist ethic of solidarity among women and workers against the individualism of the wage relation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Never discussed; adherents stress structural rights to material means and equality, and would not put duties first, particularly where duties fall on women as unpaid carers.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; modern eco-socialist feminists often affirm it, classic Marxism treats nature mainly through labour.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from left-feminist opposition to coercive population control, favouring reproductive autonomy.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Engels sees industrial wage labour as opening women's path to independence, so adherents critique capitalism rather than industry as such.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Never addressed; split between Marxist productive-forces optimism and feminist critiques of technology.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not discussed by the sources and no settled adherent view; feminist and Marxist writers differ on whether technology liberates or controls bodies.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from emphasis on democratic self-organisation.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from left suspicion of state surveillance.

restore-past-order.rationale: Engels holds that earlier orders such as mother-right were overthrown and cannot be restored; liberation comes through socialism, not return.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to a systematic structural theory.

direct-action.rationale: Dalla Costa and James call for women to refuse domestic labour and organise collectively, which is direct struggle outside parliament.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not stated; Marxist-feminist movements split between prefigurative autonomy and disciplined party organising.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Engels sees pre-class societies as holding higher status for women but looks forward to socialism, not a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Engels demands women's return to public industry and domestic work becoming a social industry, and Marxism looks to overcoming the gendered division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Classic communist principle; not discussed in the pages read, so inferred from the Marxist heritage.

production-for-use.rationale: Dalla Costa and James argue capital organises even the household for production of labour power for profit, so liberation needs production for human needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Dalla Costa and James extend Marx's analysis, arguing that capital profits from unpaid reproductive labour as well as wage labour.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Never addressed; adherents split between classical Marxist and anti-authoritarian socialist strands.

collective-farming.rationale: Not discussed in the sources read; classic Marxists favoured collective ownership but Marxist feminists did not take a position on farming.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; inferred from Marxist theory of imperialism, which Zetkin and Kollontai applied.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred: adherents want taxes to fund socialised services such as care, so calling taxation theft contradicts their programme.

harm-principle.rationale: Not discussed; adherents accept limits on liberty for equality and harm, but not the narrow liberal formulation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Inferred; adherents treat oppression as structural and group-based.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on collective organising and struggle over individual escape from oppressive structures.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from opposition to market logic in public life.

positive-liberty.rationale: Dalla Costa and James argue that women gain power through material means such as wages and freedom from unpaid work, not formal rights alone.

media-academia-power.rationale: Inferred from the view that capital and the ruling class hold real power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inferred from the materialist view of social differences.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred from rejection of family-based corporatist order.

total-state.rationale: Never addressed; adherents want collective control of production but not total state direction of life.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from the socialist critique of imperialism as a product of capitalism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from rejection of feudal hierarchy and personal dependence, which the Marxist tradition treats as relations of domination.

bound-labor.rationale: Inferred from opposition to bonded and unfree labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxist ideology critique supports it; the pages read do not state it directly.

universal-morality.rationale: Marxist treatment of morality as class-conditioned; not discussed in the pages read.

single-common-good.rationale: Inferred from class conflict view that interests are opposed.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not discussed in the sources read; Marxist and feminist writers are split, so no settled position is attributed.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; adherents have no common line on diaspora return rights.

revive-national-language.rationale: Never discussed; the topic has no connection to the core arguments on gender and class.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from Engels's goal of common ownership of production, which assumes workers control industry; the sources do not discuss company governance.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred: adherents favour public provision of social services such as education rather than market vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred: adherents want public spending on care and services and would reject deficit-avoidance as a constraint.

economic-freedom.rationale: Marxist feminists hold that formal economic freedom under capitalism rests on unpaid women's labour, so it is no basis of political freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not discussed; adherents ground authority in class power and institutions, not the moral example of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Never addressed; Marxists usually support it conditionally.

force-without-un.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from opposition to imperial wars and unilateral military action by capitalist states.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from internationalist solidarity with migrant workers.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Dalla Costa and James treat unpaid care as work and favour refusing compulsory labour, so adherents oppose compelling paid work as a condition of support.

class-collaboration.rationale: Zetkin and Kollontai rejected alliances with bourgeois women, and Marxist feminists hold interests of classes are opposed.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Never discussed; adherents would not sacrifice cultural institutions, which socialists generally want opened to the working class.

dominated-front.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; Marxist feminists have no common view on a bloc of states opposed to Western powers.

workers-nation.rationale: Marxist feminists organised working women as an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Engels argues male supremacy is an economic product and calls for women's entry into public industry, rejecting legal gender-role distinctions.

ban-interest.rationale: Never discussed; Marxist critique targets capital relations broadly, and a ban on lending is not a stated demand.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from the egalitarian and class-solidarity commitments that run against legal racial separation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Engels's Origin links the state to class society and property; the SEP presents Marxist feminists as inheriting this analysis.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from modern left positions.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from internationalism and solidarity with migrant workers, who are often women in care work.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred from rejection of conspiracy narratives.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not discussed; inferred weakly as a fairer electoral form for those seeking to organise outside the two-party system.

national-mission.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from the anti-imperialist stance against exporting a government form by power.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Engels states that the husband's supremacy in marriage is a consequence of his economic supremacy, and the world-historical defeat of the female sex; the SEP describes patriarchy as interlocking with capitalism.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from class view of political elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from opposition to eugenic coercion.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from left opposition to state repression and support for accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Marxist feminists want the state to socialise housework and childcare, which a minimal state cannot do.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from the egalitarian stance and opposition to state control of reproduction and marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Engels's critique of the unequal marriage contract assumes women's equal standing; equal rights are a basic aim.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The sources never address this debate, which concerns Soviet-era party doctrine rather than gender and class.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not discussed in the sources read; inferred from the anti-colonial leanings of the left.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian opposition to religious personal laws that disadvantage women.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from opposition to state coercion over private belief, though adherents are critical of religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Never discussed; religious dietary law is outside the core concerns and adherents would not impose it by law.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from the secular materialist outlook and its critique of religious institutions sanctifying family patriarchy.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The sources do not address this question and adherents hold mixed views on Soviet-style state strengthening.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Never directly discussed; inferred from democratic socialist commitments to rule by the working majority.

trade-surplus.rationale: Never discussed; export-surplus goals are mercantilist, which adherents would see as competition between capitalist states.

population-transfer.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from opposition to coercive state control over people, notably bodies and families.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Inferred from endorsement of revolutionary struggle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Marxist feminists see history driven by class cooperation and conflict over property, not individual competition, and reject social Darwinism.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Never discussed; Marxist movements have often been banned themselves, so adherents are wary of such powers.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Dalla Costa and James treat unwaged women's dependency as domination; the sources do not use the republican term.

separated-powers.rationale: Not discussed; Marxists treat constitutional forms as class instruments but not all reject checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Zetkin and Kollontai worked within parties, while Dalla Costa and James stress women's own autonomous organising, so adherents split.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Dalla Costa and James centre working-class women, and Marxist feminists prioritise the exploited.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Never discussed; adherents favour public housing but may be split on tenant purchase.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Early Marxist feminists organised working women in labour movements and favour strike rights.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxist analysis attributes poverty to social relations of property, not demographics.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from solidarity across lines of race and nationality as central to class unity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not discussed; rotation and sortition appear in some left thought, but not in these sources.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from opposition to expanded state coercive powers.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from support for collective control over necessities and for reproduction needs.

party-controls-media.rationale: Never discussed; autonomous women's organising implies independent media, though adherents in ruling parties differ.

party-commands-army.rationale: Never discussed; adherents are split by Soviet practice, so a mild disagreement is inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from working-class internationalism, which opposes making migrant workers wait years for equal standing.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from Marxist egalitarian precedent.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not discussed; Zetkin and Kollontai worked within parties, whereas autonomist strands reject binding discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Never discussed; Marxists favour international cooperation but distrust capitalist unions such as the EU.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from opposition to concentrated executive power over armed forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from rejection of hierarchical religious institutions.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rejected as rule by patriarchal institutions that sanction the monogamous family.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Never addressed in the pages read; Marxist anti-war tradition including Zetkin and Kollontai held it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from opposition to moral censorship, historically aimed at women and sexuality.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not discussed; the issue is not bound to class or gender analysis.

recall-officials.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from commitment to accountability of delegates to those who elected them.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from anti-militarism and opposition to blocs of capitalist powers.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Never discussed; adherents favour social housing rather than universal individual ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: Never discussed; classical Marxists favour popular militias but feminist pacifist strands disagree.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Engels expects women's liberation through entry into public industry, which implies no romanticising of rural household life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Never discussed; national division is not an issue in the gender and class analysis.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Never discussed; adherents include many academics and see this populist claim as a diversion from class.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not discussed; adherents criticise patriarchal cultural practice, so relativism is not a clear position.

death-penalty.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from socialist and feminist opposition to state killing.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from left-feminist consensus; not in sources read.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from the materialist, scientific orientation of Marxism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; feminists divide sharply, with anti-porn and sex-positive camps both existing among socialists.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from internationalism and rejection of descent-based membership.

minority-language-support.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from egalitarian support for equal access for minorities.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from concern about exemptions from equality law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not discussed; the question is liberal in origin and not addressed by Marxist feminism.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from anti-imperialism and critique of global capital.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from analogous claim that political equality needs economic change.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Never discussed; the sources do not address constitutional procedure.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Never discussed; adherents prioritise freedom from domination and would not trade it for output.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from global solidarity and critique of unequal world economy.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not discussed; Marxist feminists have no common view on head-of-state selection.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from opposition to insulating economic policy from democratic control.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from preference for negotiated settlements over territorial claims.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Engels sees private property as the origin of women's subjugation, so property should serve social ends.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The sources do not address the question and Marxist-feminist adherents are divided on the Soviet record.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Never discussed; weak inference from left support for regulating environmental risk.

collective-defense.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from opposition to capitalist military alliances such as NATO.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from anti-imperialism and respect for popular consent.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from the critique of religious institutions that sanction patriarchal family law.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Never discussed; the sources have no position on ceremonial heads of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from preference against military coercion of peoples.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Never discussed; question concerns special administrative regions with no link to the core arguments.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from materialist rejection of divine sanction for rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from preference for progressive redistribution.

character-from-environment.rationale: Engels, quoting Morgan, says the family is a creature of the social system; Marxist feminists hold gendered character is formed by social conditions.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from opposition to unaccountable power.

space-expansion.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from priority on social needs over a space programme.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Never discussed; Marxist feminists favour majority working-class rule, not balance with elites.

leader-cult.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from rejection of personality politics and from autonomous mass organising.

equal-parenting.rationale: Ferguson's council-socialist vision proposes shared caring work, implying equal parenting responsibilities, though not about court presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Never addressed by Marxist feminists; Marxists are divided.

land-redistribution.rationale: Never discussed in these sources; inferred from opposition to concentrated property in land.

refugee-return.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from solidarity with displaced people.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from internationalism and rejection of ethnic territorial claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from opposition to religious coercion, particularly against women.

women-must-cover.rationale: Opposes laws fixing women's subordinate status, consistent with Engels's insistence on equality in public life.

common-currency.rationale: Never discussed; no common position on monetary unions.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from preference for class over ethnic-linguistic unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Never discussed; the sources have no position on minority cultural self-government.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Never discussed; this is a Jewish-political debate not addressed by these sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Engels derives the family and women's status from changes in property and production, as Origin of the Family argues.

ban-cartels.rationale: Never addressed; adherents want ownership change, not competition policy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Never discussed; adherents oppose bailouts of banks but support public rescue of jobs and services.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Never discussed; adherents want majority control but also protection against patriarchal majority rule.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Marxist feminists favour women's participation in public life, though some see quotas as insufficient or elite-serving.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from rejection of autarkic imperial blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from concern for labour standards, including for women workers.

moral-incentives.rationale: Never discussed; this is a Guevarist Marxist idea, and inferred mild support from communist heritage.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on mass self-organisation of women and workers, not small armed vanguards.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Engels ties women's subjugation to patriarchal inheritance of property, so abolishing hereditary privilege follows.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from internationalism and critical, non-nationalist history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from anti-colonial stance.

patriotic-education.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from internationalism and critique of nationalist ideology.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Never discussed; adherents prioritise class measures but mostly support remedying racial disadvantage.

public-money-creation.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from preference for public control of finance.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Never addressed; adherents see capitalism adapting by using unpaid women's labour.

delink-world-market.rationale: Never discussed; dependency-theory debates split Marxists on delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Never discussed in the sources; Marxists are divided on the thesis.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from opposition to discrimination against women.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Never discussed; adherents want rights but doubt constitutions under capitalism protect them.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from anti-colonial stance.

elective-rulers.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from rejection of hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from majoritarian class politics and distrust of veto powers that block redistribution.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Never discussed; endorsement of revolutionary action implies a right to resist unjust rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Never discussed; Marxists treat parliaments as limited class-bound institutions.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Never discussed; weak inference from left-feminist ethics, which often extend care to animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Never discussed; no common adherent position.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from rejection of paternalistic charity.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Dalla Costa and James call for women's collective organising and the personal made political.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marxist ideology critique supports it; not stated in the pages read.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony view; not stated in the pages read.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Never discussed in the sources read; inferred from the Marxist account of imperialism and global exploitation, including of women in the global south.

native-born-offices.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from internationalism and opposition to citizenship-based exclusion.

party-own-road.rationale: Never discussed; this concerns communist party strategy, on which adherents differ.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from rejection of territorial nationalism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Never discussed; adherents are mixed between decolonial support and class-universal politics.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from the left's historical anti-fascism, including of Zetkin.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Never discussed; Marxist feminists reject equating communism with fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Never discussed; Marxist historiography treats slavery as central.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from left support for removing honours of oppressors.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Never addressed; adherents likely agree attention is warranted but frame it as class issues.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from the structural account of male power, which treats violence by men as the dominant pattern.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from universalist emancipatory aims.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from opposition to political role for armies.

paid-care-work.rationale: Dalla Costa and James demand wages for housework, while Engels prefers socialising it, so the strands split.

filial-duty.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the aim of socialising care.

office-by-exam.rationale: Never discussed; the sources have no position on how civil service posts are filled.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Never discussed; adherents oppose capital concentration but not nationalistically.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Engels writes that if only marriage based on love is moral, so is only the marriage in which love continues, and that when affection ends 'separation is a benefit for both partners'.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Never discussed in sources read; inferred from council-socialist emphasis on delegate accountability.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from preference for collective provision, and since women's gaps in paid work make individual accounts disadvantageous.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from preference for common ownership of land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Never discussed; the sources have no position on parliamentary budget control.

single-official-language.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from egalitarian respect for minorities.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Never discussed; adherents oppose concentrated landownership but the sources do not address foreign owners.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from structural analysis of inequality.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from Marxist critique of commodity culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from anti-imperialist rejection of covert intervention by great powers.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from opposition to great-power interference in other countries' affairs.

corporate-influence.rationale: Dalla Costa and James and the wider Marxist tradition see capital as dominating social life, so corporate power over government is an expected case of capital's power.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Never discussed; the sources have no position on foreign funding of NGOs.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state control of reproduction.

residents-only-property.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from preference for universal housing rights over exclusion.

job-guarantee.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from support for full employment and women's access to waged work, which Engels sees as a precondition of liberation.

democratic-peace.rationale: Never discussed; Marxists tie war to capitalism rather than regime type.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Never discussed; adherents view law as class-based but not all deny a duty.

non-intervention.rationale: Never discussed; adherents oppose imperial intervention but support solidarity.

industrial-unions.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from the Marxist preference for broad class unions over craft divisions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Never discussed; rejected as a conspiracy theory that diverts from class analysis.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Engels ties legal monogamous marriage to property and expects it to lose its economic function; adherents differ on abolishing the institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from democratic accountability.

local-production.rationale: Never discussed; the sources have no position on localised production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Dalla Costa and James stress autonomous, self-organised women's groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Never discussed; the sources have no position on the primacy of national law.

religious-nation.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from secular, internationalist class politics.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from redistributive solidarity across regions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marxism distinguishes personal from productive property; not in pages read.

defeat-communism.rationale: Never discussed; adherents belong to the communist and socialist tradition.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Never discussed; adherents want care provided publicly and socially, not marketised.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxist view, inferred; not discussed in sources read.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Engels sees capitalism drawing women into public industry, creating a precondition for liberation, while denying it delivers it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Engels states the wife's liberation requires women's return to public industry and the abolition of capitalist production; Marxist feminism is defined by this claim.

socialized-care.rationale: Engels states that private housekeeping is transformed into a social industry and care of children becomes a public matter.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Never discussed; linguistic purism is alien to the internationalist outlook.

treaties-binding.rationale: Never discussed; the sources have no position on treaties with nations within a state.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Never discussed; adherents prefer social transformation at scale, though cooperative forms appear in some utopian strands.

majority-settlement.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from rejection of ethnic demographic engineering.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Engels expects liberation only under common ownership, so a third way is rejected.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from preference for people's present needs over historical claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Never discussed; rejected as false and associated with fascism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Never discussed in the sources; inferred from opposition to state regulation of sexuality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from preference for popular self-organisation.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from secular, anti-clerical stance.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Never discussed; unrelated to the core arguments of Marxist feminism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Never discussed; rejected as a religious-law doctrine opposed to secular egalitarianism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on women's self-organisation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Dalla Costa and James reject treating women's oppression as separate from class; the SEP records debates on class and sex class, with class primary for most.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Never addressed in sources read; modern adherents lean supportive though some disagree.

assisted-dying.rationale: Never discussed; adherents have no common line on this.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Marxist feminism treats class conflict as the main division.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's alienation is part of the Marxist heritage that Marxist feminists extend to unwaged reproductive work, though pages read do not use the term.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Never discussed; rejected as a cultural essentialism that cuts across class solidarity.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from the secular, materialist outlook.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Never discussed; secularists and anti-racist feminists divide on this.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from feminist concern with workplace power.

social-market-economy.rationale: Adherents see it as retaining capitalism, which they hold entrenches women's unpaid work.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from anti-militarism, though many Marxists accept defensive forces.

rich-first.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from egalitarian rejection of unequal development justified by trickle-down.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Never discussed; adherents differ on whether to side with socialist states.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Engels ties hereditary succession through male line to patriarchal property.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Never discussed; this is a mutualist idea not taken up by Marxist feminism.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from opposition to austerity that increases women's unpaid care burden.

property-franchise.rationale: Engels treats property as the basis of class and male power, so property qualifications are rejected.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The socialist ecofeminist link is a later extension; classical Marxist feminism centres on class and capital, though Engels and Marx both discuss domination.

reification.rationale: Marxist feminism rests on Marx's account of capital, where social relations appear as relations between things, and its domestic-labour arguments apply that analysis to women's work.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marxist tradition treats bourgeois freedoms as formal while capital holds the means of communication; the feminist sources here do not discuss the press directly.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Marxist feminists see law as an instrument of class and patriarchal power, but also want legal equality; the sources give no clear view.

racial-franchise.rationale: Socialist feminism is internationalist and anti-racist; inferred, as the sources do not discuss voting by race.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic and not discussed; the tradition's emphasis is on organising in workplaces and communities, so no clear inference.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's call for democratic accountability to working people; not discussed.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Engels favoured marriage free of property and legal compulsion; restricting it by religion would be seen as a control on women, inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from Marxist feminism's class-solidarity internationalism, which opposes dividing workers by religion; not discussed.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Marxist feminists prefer mass organisation and workers' councils to randomly selected panels, but no source addresses sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Marxist feminism treats religion as part of the ideology sustaining women's subordination; reform versus rejection is not addressed in the sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Marxist feminists see capital's power over labour and the state as the root of unfreedom, so concentrated wealth is a threat to liberty, though their focus is class power rather than the liberty framing.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred: socialist feminists generally oppose sexual-orientation discrimination as part of the wider liberation of women and workers; the sources do not address military service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: Marxist feminists treat religion as an ideology of the old order but locate liberation in changing material conditions, not in state-run unbelief; the sources do not address it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: Marxist feminists see the state as the instrument of class rule, and abolitionist feminism has grown in the socialist-feminist tradition, though earlier strands did not demand it.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: the framework is class-based and rejects communal divisions as the organising principle of politics, so guaranteed communal shares are not a goal.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: They argue care work must be socialised and provided publicly rather than left to private households and charity, which keeps women's unpaid labour in place.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and not a concern of the tradition; adherents have no settled view on term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents who favour council democracy might welcome recallable delegates, but the tradition has no settled position on delegable voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: the tradition puts present exploitation and unequal social reproduction first, and would treat extinction risk as secondary to ending capitalism.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the demand for women's full equality and liberation; the sources do not discuss religious office.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Engels describes the monogamous family as founded on the open or concealed domestic slavery of the wife and the husband as ruling it, and calls for equality of the spouses.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the internationalist, class-based outlook that defines the political community by labour rather than citizenship.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the focus on social reproduction and housing costs borne by working women; not discussed directly.

abolish-ip.rationale: Marxist analysis targets private property in the means of production; its stance on patents is not stated.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: socialist youth leagues existed, but a national-service purpose conflicts with internationalism.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the internationalist, anti-militarist tradition of Zetkin.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Engels ties women's subjugation to private property, and the tradition holds that value comes from labour, so ownership alone should not earn income.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: the tradition accepts revolutionary and defensive force, though the sources do not discuss the specific claim.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from historical materialism, which sees nations as products of modern class and economic development.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Socialist feminists distinguish sex from gender, but not all take the further step; not stated.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Dalla Costa and James treat women as a shared class by housework, but the tradition emphasises class divisions among women.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the secular, materialist outlook.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Historical materialism explains politics through class interests and material conditions, not spiritual struggle.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from historical materialism, which puts material conditions before culture.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the critique of religion as supporting patriarchy, though materialists treat language about God as secondary.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Engels sees religion and family as supports of subjugation, so a test of women's humanity is consistent; not stated directly.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and the class-over-nation outlook, which rejects economic life organised by national group.

independent-unions.rationale: Marxist feminists back organising in the labour movement, but Marxist-Leninist traditions accepted party-led unions, so adherents split.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Engels and the socialist women's movement treat working-class rule as the point of socialism and the condition for women's liberation.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Marxist feminists demand socialised care and public provision of services, though they would favour public ownership generally, not local specifically.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's preference for unified councils and sovereign working-class assemblies over checks and balances.

municipal-property.rationale: The tradition calls for social ownership of the means of production at the level of society and class, not specifically community ownership against the state.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from council communists to statists.

family-wage.rationale: Marxist feminists criticise the male-breadwinner family as a vehicle of women's dependence and demand women's entry into public industry or wages for housework.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; no doctrine on drug approval and the sources do not address it.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition would favour public research funding but has no specific position on ageing.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from preference for democratic public control of finance, and distrust of untraceable private money.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents are split between privacy against state and corporate surveillance and concern over online harassment.

person-over-state.rationale: Marxist feminism holds that the state serves class rule and wants liberation of persons, but rejects liberal individualism, so adherents answer neither way.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Historical materialism treats religion as ideology and Engels treats it as a prop of the patriarchal family, so a spiritual-nature claim is not endorsed.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition has no doctrine on regional autonomy.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; Marxist feminism does not address crop technology, and views would depend on who controls it.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; socialist tradition favours socialised housework in collective housing, but environmental claims about density are not part of it.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The tradition prioritises class solidarity across lines; its later anti-racist strands acknowledge distinct experience, so it is disagree only weakly.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed by the core sources; classical Marxists treat race as secondary to class while later strands defend minority pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Socialist feminists were largely anti-war, but Marxist doctrine supports revolutionary and national liberation wars, so adherents split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: Marxist feminism puts class before nation and follows internationalist socialism, so a nation defined by shared language is not endorsed.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: the tradition favours secular, common political institutions and class organisation across communities, not separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: the analysis locates oppression in class and family relations, not foreign plots; the sources do not discuss the claim.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the demand to socialise housework, care and education so women are freed from private household burdens; tuition is not discussed directly.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: Marxist feminists see capitalism itself as the cause of exploitation, so a tax within the market is unlikely to be seen as the main remedy.

future-generations.rationale: Anachronistic for the founders; inferred from the socialist concern with social reproduction and sustaining life for later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Marxist feminists generally reject views that women are naturally distinct, tracing differences to class and the division of labour; the sources discuss this only indirectly.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from the socialist women's movement of Zetkin and Kollontai, which was internationalist and anti-war, though arms levels are not addressed directly.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: Bolshevik-era socialists denounced secret treaties; the feminist sources do not discuss diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalism and support for state direction of the economy; the sources do not address capital movements.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Marxist feminists see the state's army and police as instruments of class rule, not neutral monopolists of force; inferred from the Marxist theory of the state.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Marxist tradition, including Zetkin and Kollontai, opposed inter-imperialist war and urged workers not to fight it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Marxist feminists support unions and collective action, including organising women workers, over individual contracts, though they see bargaining as insufficient.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: tax credits subsidise low wages and leave capitalism and unpaid domestic labour intact, whereas Marxist feminists want to socialise care.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from opposition to austerity and demand for public provision of care and childcare.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Marxist analysis of imperialism implies support, but the tradition centres on class and gender within capitalism; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Engels saw the state as an instrument of class rule that socialism must replace, but strands differ on reform versus rupture.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Marxist feminists have a definite programme of socialised production and care, not open experiments; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not a core topic; Marxist critique treats commodification as capitalist, but ecological Marxists differ; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: Marxist feminism is internationalist and sees nationalism as a tool that divides the working class and reinforces patriarchal family roles.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from support for free public education and opposition to debt burdens on workers.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Marxist analysis of uneven development is compatible, but the tradition focuses on class and gender, so adherents are split; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Marxists hold that human nature is historically formed by social relations, and feminists reject fixed natures that justify gender roles; Engels traces the family historically.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from opposition to capitalist ownership of media; adherents would doubt that state-funded media is fully independent.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Marxism treats religion as ideology tied to class society, so a committed Marxist feminist would not affirm that all religions share one truth; inferred from the tradition's materialism.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from socialist support for state protection of small producers against capital and creditors; the tradition rarely addresses farm policy directly.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the socialist-feminist left's anti-militarism and preference for redirecting resources to social provision.

workers-own-party.rationale: Zetkin and Kollontai built independent working-class women's organisation and rejected alliance with bourgeois parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from opposition to violence against women; the tradition seldom addresses FGM specifically and some strands stress anti-imperialist caution.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Engels names women's legal equality and economic independence as preconditions of liberation, though the tradition holds legal rights alone are insufficient.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic classification question the tradition never addresses; no position can be inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from preference for collective and social control of production over individualist property-based remedies.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from opposition to inherited, hierarchical authority and to institutions tied to patriarchal property relations.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from socialist critiques of capitalist externalities; the tradition rarely frames the trade-off against liberty.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the left's general scepticism of punitive criminal justice and its focus on social causes of crime.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The tradition never addresses this; internationalism and concern for migrant women workers pull against assimilationist requirements.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Anachronistic as a feminist question; inferred from Marxist support for strong unions as vehicles of working-class power.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from socialist concern that such requirements burden poorer and marginalized voters.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the socialist tradition of a secular state that privileges no church.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Engels treats bourgeois formal equality as masking class domination, so electoral procedure alone is not real democracy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Engels argues monogamy rooted in property should give way to sexual relations based on mutual inclination, free of economic compulsion.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from socialist-feminist support for free communication and organizing, though not a core topic.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Anachronistic; the tradition favors socialized services and a wage for housework debate over a cash payment replacing welfare.

women-suffrage.rationale: The socialist women's movement of Zetkin and Kollontai demanded equal political rights, and the tradition treats women's full part in public life as essential.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Engels links women's subjection to property and the family, with religion as part of the ideological superstructure that sustains it, though capital is the main cause.

race-social-construct.rationale: Marxist feminists treat race as a socially produced category tied to capitalist and colonial relations, rather than a natural division.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the demand for public provision of care; dalla Costa and James would doubt that state agencies can substitute for transformation.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Engels's account that private property is the root of women's subjugation, so claim-based ownership is not a principle.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the view of law as an instrument of the ruling class; the sources do not address international criminal courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the materialist tradition's view of religion as ideology, not a source of literal truth.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to women's full participation in public life and production.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: the tradition looks to the socialised-property state of the Soviet experiment, but strands disagree about bureaucratic rule.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the socialist tradition's council and delegate structures, though the sources do not discuss them directly.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the materialist critique of religion and the tradition's support for equality before the law.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the socialist movement's support for national self-determination and equal rights of nationalities.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the socialist support for the self-determination of peoples, though the sources do not address plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialism of the socialist tradition; the sources do not address borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the aim of socialising housework through modern production and abundance rather than self-sufficient household labour.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: The sources do not address it, and socialist anti-colonialism and universalism pull in opposite directions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the demand for women's equality in public life and production.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: Marxist feminism is materialist and internationalist, so a spiritual tie between a nation and its land is not part of its analysis.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's concern with the state's power over the poor; no source addresses killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition is anti-imperialist toward all great powers and adherents differ on China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred: the tradition is internationalist and organises across borders by class, not through kin-state protection of ethnic minorities.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Engels ties women's subjugation to private property and calls for the means of production to become common property.

self-ownership.rationale: Adherents split: they reject liberal ownership of labour power as a commodity, yet press for women's control of their own bodies.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: broad consumption taxes fall hardest on poorer households, which a class analysis opposes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: the case for socialised care and housework points to universal public provision rather than means-tested help.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Zetkin and Kollontai organised working women through labour movements and parties, not around them.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred: favours to well-connected firms are capitalist privilege that Marxist analysis opposes.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred: the tradition is secular and class-based, and sees religious communal politics as reinforcing patriarchal family law.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: reviving ancestral values would revive the patriarchal family that Engels traces to property society.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Engels holds that marriage should rest on free affection and be dissolved when affection ends, and the tradition demands women's legal equality in marriage.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: Marxist feminists favour social control of wealth, and national control is a step away from foreign capital.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Engels and the Marxist tradition judge property relations by their class outcomes, not by whether each exchange was voluntary.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred: a levy on speculative finance fits the anti-capitalist programme, though the sources do not discuss it.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Many Marxist and socialist feminists stress racism's structural effects, but the core sources centre on class and gender, so the answer is inferred.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition judges law as a class instrument but its adherents have no common line on obedience.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Dalla Costa and James advocate refusal of work and Marxist feminists want housework socialised, which implies less toil; machinery is inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold varied views on the great powers.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Dalla Costa and James argue that housework produces the value of labour power, which rests on the Marxist view that labour creates value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Zetkin and Kollontai put class solidarity across borders ahead of national loyalty, so patriotism is seen as dividing workers.

material-over-identity.rationale: Marxist feminists insist women's oppression is a distinct part of the class struggle, so they do not set it aside for narrowly economic demands.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split over whether markets under party rule are socialism.

missingStatements.text: Housework should be recognised as productive labour that capitalism depends on.
missingStatements.rationale: Central claim of Dalla Costa and James: housework produces labour power, the commodity capital buys, so unpaid domestic work is part of capitalist production.

missingStatements.text: Women's oppression originated with the rise of private property and inheritance.
missingStatements.rationale: Engels argues men overthrew mother-right to pass property to their own children, the world-historical defeat of the female sex.

missingStatements.text: Women's liberation requires bringing the whole female sex back into public industry.
missingStatements.rationale: Engels calls this the first condition for the liberation of the wife; the SEP records it as the classic Marxist position.

missingStatements.text: Feminists should ally with working-class movements rather than with women of the ruling class.
missingStatements.rationale: Zetkin and Kollontai rejected cross-class alliances because bourgeois women benefit from working-class women's labour.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow Marxist-feminist strategy question about class alliances; no other audits proposed it and the bank is kept lean.

notes: Strands differ on wages for housework (Dalla Costa, James, Federici) versus socialisation of care (Engels, Vogel); on dual systems (Hartmann) versus a single capitalist system; and on sex work and pornography. The answers for non-gender topics are mostly inferred from the Marxist heritage and are low confidence.
